record.paper_title: Operations Research challenges in forestry: 33 open problems
record.original_question: On-board bucking computers use internal price lists to direct logs into diameter-length classes, but the literature has not addressed how such internal prices should be managed across multiple harvest areas. The open question is how to design and use pricing schemes as an explicit coordination mechanism for operational forest decisions.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5 How can we use pricing as a coordination mechanism for forest operations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In mechanized timber harvesting, a harvester equipped with an on-board bucking computer cross-cuts each felled stem into logs assigned to diameter–length classes. The bucking decision at each stem is driven by an internal price list that assigns a value to every (diameter class, length class) combination; the on-board optimizer selects the cutting pattern that maximizes the total internal value of the logs produced from the stem. When several harvest areas operate in parallel and feed multiple downstream demand points (mills, terminals, customer orders) with possibly differing product mixes, capacities, and time windows, the choice of internal price lists across stands becomes a coordination instrument: it determines, indirectly, the realized product assortment, inventories, and transport flows.

Formulate a general framework for using such internal prices as an explicit coordination mechanism for operational forest decisions. Concretely:

1. Define a model in which a central planner (or a market-style mechanism) chooses, for each harvest area $h$ in a set $H$ and each time period $t$, a price list $p_{h,t}:D\times L\to\mathbb{R}$, where $D$ is the set of diameter classes and $L$ the set of length classes. Each stem $s$ harvested in area $h$ at time $t$ is bucked according to $\arg\max$ of $\sum p_{h,t}(d,\ell)\cdot x_{s}(d,\ell)$ subject to the geometric/taper feasibility constraints on the cutting pattern $x_s$.

2. Identify conditions on $\{p_{h,t}\}$ under which the resulting aggregate supply of log classes solves (or approximately solves) a global operational optimization problem that maximizes total value (revenue minus harvesting, storage, and transportation cost) subject to mill demands, capacity, and inventory constraints, in the spirit of duality / Lagrangian decomposition for the global problem.

3. Determine whether prices can be updated dynamically (e.g., by subgradient or auction-type procedures) using only locally observable harvest information so as to converge to a coordinated optimum, and characterize the loss of optimality compared to a fully centralized bucking-and-distribution model.

Provide such a pricing-based coordination scheme together with a theoretical or computational analysis of its optimality, convergence, and information requirements.
artifact.category_tag: Forestry operations research and pricing coordination
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g., integrated bucking-and-routing models and tactical forest-sawmill planning) addresses joint optimization of bucking, transportation, and demand, but treats price lists as inputs rather than as a designed coordination mechanism across multiple harvest areas. No work was found that resolves the general question of designing and dynamically managing internal harvester price lists as an explicit operational coordination tool. The problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Supply network planning in the forest supply chain with bucking decisions anticipation
status_evidence.snippet: Bucking and distribution decisions are usually considered separately, giving rise to suboptimal solutions.
status_evidence.claim: Coordination between bucking and downstream decisions remains an active modelling challenge.

status_evidence.title: An Integrated Approach for Solving the Bucking and Routing Problems in the Forest Industry
status_evidence.snippet: Integrated mathematical programming models for bucking with transportation and market demands.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work integrates bucking with routing but does not address pricing as a coordination mechanism across stands.

status_evidence.title: Optimization in forest operations and supply chains
status_evidence.snippet: Mechanized harvesters use on-board bucking optimization software given a price list for different log types.
status_evidence.claim: Internal price lists drive on-board bucking decisions but their cross-area management is not standardized.
